scope: production implementation of the minimum per-host extraction override engine selected by certified Phase 4E, without adding site-specific rules

configuration_contract.encoding: JSON list of rule objects parsed by Settings
configuration_contract.default_behavior: an empty rule list preserves the certified global extraction path

rule_schema.host: required exact DNS hostname; normalize to lowercase and remove one or more trailing dots; schemes, ports, paths, credentials, wildcards, empty labels and IP literals are rejected
rule_schema.remove_selectors: optional list of 1 to 32 non-empty CSS selector strings, each at most 512 characters; default empty

rule_validation: a rule that enables neither remove_selectors nor force_browser is rejected

matching_contract.url_source: FetchResult.final_url after the certified fetch/redirect path completes
matching_contract.precedence: none; normalized host keys are unique so at most one rule can match

remove_selectors_contract.ordering: custom removals occur before the worker's existing global cleanup selectors and before Mozilla Readability
remove_selectors_contract.atomicity: all configured selectors are resolved before any custom DOM mutation; if any selector is syntactically invalid, no configured selector removal is applied for that extraction
remove_selectors_contract.invalid_selector_behavior: fail open to the existing unmodified-by-custom-rules Readability path
remove_selectors_contract.worker_failure_behavior: preserve the existing Python fallback path; custom selector rules do not make worker failure fatal and do not alter Trafilatura fallback semantics
remove_selectors_contract.payload_scope: the Python extractor sends remove_selectors only for the matched rule

force_browser_contract.trigger: a matched rule with force_browser=true requests the existing render-extract path even when the global quality heuristic would not request browser rendering
force_browser_contract.browser_enabled: the request is attempted only when the existing global browser_enabled setting is true
force_browser_contract.browser_disabled_behavior: return the existing static extraction without error
force_browser_contract.render_failure_behavior: return the existing static extraction without error
force_browser_contract.render_success_selection: a valid rendered extraction replaces the static extraction regardless of the existing quality/length comparison; this mirrors the certified Phase 4E candidate semantics
force_browser_contract.heuristic_behavior_without_force: when no matched rule forces rendering, the existing _needs_browser trigger and rendered-is-better selection remain unchanged
force_browser_contract.security: force_browser does not bypass validatePublicUrl, request interception, SSRF controls, browser_enabled, fetcher policy, robots policy, or any existing browser security behavior

combined_rule_contract.behavior: when one matched rule contains both primitives, remove_selectors is applied to both the static and rendered Readability inputs and force_browser controls whether the rendered path is requested/selected
combined_rule_contract.failure_isolation: an invalid remove selector fails open for selector mutation but does not suppress an otherwise eligible force_browser request

matching: subdomain does not inherit parent rule
requested/original host does not override final redirected host
canonical URL does not influence matching
remove_selectors: no matched rule preserves baseline output
valid selector removes preregistered noise while preserving required content
mixed valid plus invalid selectors are baseline-equivalent, proving atomic fail-open
the same cleanup function is exercised on frozen static and rendered fixture HTML
force_browser: matched force_browser requests rendering even when _needs_browser is false
successful forced render is selected even if shorter or lower-scored than static
unmatched/non-forced extraction retains existing heuristic selection semantics
regression: full existing 9-workflow matrix passes on the policy-only head
full existing 9-workflow matrix passes on the functional implementation head
